name: Sichuan, China
summary: Pandas at opening time, a bronze-age mystery pit, an ancient irrigation works, and a valley of coloured lakes. The most unusual education in this set, with a visa question mark for 2027.
why: The 12- and 14-year-olds get Sanxingdui and Dujiangyan, which are real science and history. The 6-year-old gets pandas and a boardwalk valley. You can do it from Chengdu plus two side bases, by train and one short flight. A 14-day loop through Beijing, Xi'an and Zhangjiajie adds the famous sights and spends the holiday changing cities. That loop is not this plan.
distinctive: A conservation centre for giant pandas beside an archaeological site that rewrote early Chinese history, and a high valley of mineral lakes.
weather: Chengdu in April is often mild and cloudy, roughly the mid-teens to mid-20s. Jiuzhaigou's valley is cooler. One spring guide cited about 11–24°C there in a past April. Nights at the park towns are cold. This is seasonal, not a forecast.
crowds: Jiuzhaigou's own 2026 peak-season notice set a daily capacity of 41,000 and full-valley opening from 1 April, with entry 08:00–14:00. Capacity that high means the park can still feel busy. The calmer aim is the middle of April, after Qingming and before the Labour Day holiday. The 2027 holiday dates need the State Council notice.
natureExperiences: Jiuzhaigou's lakes and waterfalls, using the park buses rather than trying to walk the whole valley
Dujiangyan and the wooded paths of nearby Qingcheng Mountain, kept short
A dawn visit to the Chengdu panda base
Leshan's river cliff and giant Buddha, seen without rushing the same day as Chengdu
age6: Pandas first, then the Jiuzhaigou buses and short boardwalks. Skip Huanglong. It sits higher, around 3,000 metres.
age12: Sanxingdui's masks, the panda science, and the coloured lakes.
age14: Dujiangyan's 2,000-year-old flood works, Sanxingdui, and the question of how a landscape makes lakes that colour.
adults: Teahouses, the archaeology, and a national park that does not look like anywhere else. Sichuan food is spicy. Ask for mild plates for the children.
gettingAround: High-speed rail for Leshan. A flight of about an hour from Chengdu to Jiuzhai Huanglong Airport, then a ground transfer of about 1–1.5 hours. Confirm both in 2027. China drives on the right. You do not need a car for this plan.
meetingPoint: Chengdu Tianfu or Shuangliu. A July 2026 route listing showed no nonstop Bengaluru–Chengdu flight, only one-stop journeys. Melbourne is also usually one stop. This is the more even journey of the top options. Meet in Chengdu. Do not send the Bengaluru party through Melbourne. Recheck the 2027 timetable. Give the later arrival a free first afternoon.
visaAu: In February 2026, China's visa-free entry for ordinary Australian passports, for up to 30 days and for tourism, was described as running until 31 December 2026. April 2027 is after that date. Unless Beijing extends it, the Australian party will need a visa too. Do not book as if the waiver still exists.
visaIn: India was not on that visa-free list. Indian passports should plan on a tourist visa. The 240-hour transit scheme is not a way to spend two weeks in Sichuan, and Jiuzhaigou's prefecture has been excluded from some transit areas. Use a proper visa.
disadvantages: The Australian visa waiver, as published, expires before this trip. Both passport groups should plan on visas until an extension is official.
Jiuzhaigou's entrance is about 1,990 metres. The park says altitude sickness is uncommon and still possible. Take the first afternoon slowly. Skip Huanglong with a 6-year-old.
The food is part of the pleasure and a problem for cautious children. Build in plain rice, dumplings and mild dishes.
English is thinner on the ground than in Japan or New Zealand. Offline maps and the hotel card in Chinese matter.
uncertainties: Whether the Australian 30-day waiver is extended past 31 December 2026.
The 2027 Qingming and Labour Day holiday lengths.
Jiuzhaigou ticket rules and which lakes are open in April 2027. Read en.jiuzhai.com the month you book.

gain: The strangest and most educational mix: living animals, ancient engineering, and a lake valley.
miss: A settled visa rule for April 2027, and the ease of travelling with young children in English.

cost.summary: Melbourne fares about ₹1.3–1.8 lakh for three adults. A typical Bengaluru fare for the group was not published, so there is no combined flight total. The Chinese visa fees on file expire 31 December 2026. Hotels and food are not included.

lines.text: Kayak.com.au’s typical return fare, Melbourne to Chengdu, was A$665–$917 for one adult. Three adult fares are about ₹1.3–1.8 lakh. One stop. Not an April 2027 quote.
On 7 October 2026 a cheapest round trip was advertised at US$529 for one adult on a November date. That is one deal, not a typical price, so it is not multiplied by four.

The reduced fees were published only through 31 December 2026. At the Delhi centre an Indian regular single entry was ₹2,900 plus a ₹2,107 service fee. In Sydney an Australian regular single entry was A$94.50 in total. April 2027 is after that date. Do not use those figures as the fee you will pay.

cost.leftOut: Hotels, meals, trains, the Jiuzhaigou flight and park tickets are not included.

trip.band: about ₹4–9 lakh before the Bengaluru flights
trip.note: Only the Melbourne flights are inside this. The four Bengaluru tickets, and the 2027 visa fee, are not.
trip.text: A band for seven people and about 13 nights, rounded to the nearest lakh. Not a quote, and not used to order the list. Three rooms, meals for seven, local transport and tickets. The 6-year-old's meals are not discounted. Insurance, bags and shopping are outside it. The columns are Chengdu's, from Budget Your Trip on 4 September 2026. A Jiuzhaigou hotel can differ. A typical Bengaluru fare was not published, so it is not in the band.

stretch16: Add a free day in Chengdu and a free day at Jiuzhaigou. Do not add Beijing.

days.experience: Land and walk People's Park or a nearby teahouse.
days.optional: Map the panda morning for tomorrow and go to sleep
days.highlight: A city of teahouses used as recovery
days.kids: Playground if one is close. No museum today.
days.transfer: Both families fly into Chengdu. Allow for a long airport transfer.
days.seasonal: Air quality varies. Have an indoor backup for the first day without treating it as an emergency.

days.experience: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding at opening.
days.optional: The red panda paths if the children still have legs
days.highlight: Pandas while they are active, which means early
days.kids: All three ages. Leave by late morning. The animals sleep and the paths fill up.
days.transfer: About 10–15 kilometres from central Chengdu. A taxi or metro-plus-taxi. Official March–October morning entry starts at 7:30.
days.seasonal: Book ahead. The base's own site is panda.org.cn.
days.wet: Go anyway. Pandas do not mind drizzle. Take a light coat.

days.optional: The bronze masks are the whole point. Do not add a second museum.
days.highlight: A pit culture with masks and trees of bronze that still surprise archaeologists
days.kids: The 6-year-old will take the faces and the scale. The 12- and 14-year-olds can take the labels.
days.transfer: About 40–60 minutes from Chengdu. Confirm the 2027 rail or museum shuttle.
days.seasonal: Weekends draw local families. A weekday is kinder.

days.experience: Dujiangyan irrigation system, and a short walk at Qingcheng only if energy remains.
days.optional: Skip the mountain and keep the water works
days.highlight: A flood-control system still in use after more than 2,000 years
days.kids: The models and the river splitting in two are the lesson. Qingcheng's stairs are optional.
days.transfer: Under an hour by fast train or car from Chengdu. Confirm the station.
days.seasonal: This is a day trip, not a new hotel.
days.wet: The irrigation museum and the covered walkways. Skip the mountain.

days.experience: A free day. Jinli or Kuanzhai for an hour, then a cooking class that includes mild dishes.
days.optional: Chengdu Museum if it is raining
days.highlight: Learning to order food, which is the local skill
days.kids: Dumplings they help shape. Chili on the side.
days.seasonal: Teahouse culture is the adult pleasure. Give it an hour, not a schedule.
days.wet: The museum and the cooking class.

days.experience: Train to Leshan and see the Giant Buddha in the late afternoon if the light and the queue allow, or the next morning.
days.optional: The river view from the cliff path
days.highlight: A seated Buddha carved into a cliff above the rivers
days.kids: There are stairs. Take the route that matches the 6-year-old, and do not combine this with a same-day return to Chengdu.
days.transfer: Chengdu to Leshan by high-speed train is often about an hour, plus a local ride to the Buddha. Confirm 2027 times.
days.seasonal: Go early on the Buddha morning. Midday tour groups are the crowd.
days.wet: The statue is outdoors. A light rain is fine. A storm is a reason to wait for the next morning.

days.experience: A slower Buddha morning if you did not finish, then a free afternoon.
days.kids: Park time or the hotel pool if it has one.
days.seasonal: Use the spare hours if the train was delayed yesterday.

days.experience: Back to Chengdu. Rest and repack for the mountains.
days.optional: A last mild hotpot for the adults, with a plain pot for the children
days.highlight: A buffer before the altitude change
days.transfer: About an hour back by train.
days.seasonal: Do not fly to Jiuzhaigou the same day you climb the Buddha stairs.
days.wet: This is already an indoor day.

days.experience: Fly to Jiuzhai Huanglong and transfer to the park town. Walk nowhere ambitious.
days.optional: Look at the entrance area only
days.kids: Watch for headaches. The park's own note says drink water and avoid hard exercise. Oxygen is sold at the entrance clinic if needed.
days.transfer: Flight about an hour, then about 1–1.5 hours by road. These are typical figures. Confirm.
days.seasonal: Peak season on the park's notices starts 1 April. Book the entry slot before you fly.
days.wet: Settle in. The park day is tomorrow.

days.experience: One full park day on the sightseeing buses. Pick a few lakes, not every boardwalk.
days.optional: Five Flower Lake and one waterfall
days.highlight: Blue, green and gold water in a forest valley
days.kids: Buses between stops are how a 6-year-old sees this park. Do not try to hike it.
days.transfer: Inside the park, the bus ticket is separate from entry. The 2026 peak notice listed entry and a bus fare. Recheck 2027 prices rather than budgeting from that notice.
days.seasonal: Last entry has been early afternoon in peak season, with the park closing at 18:00. Read the current notice.
days.wet: The colours survive cloud. Heavy rain makes boardwalks slippery. Take it slower.

days.experience: A second, shorter park visit to the corner you missed, or a free morning.
days.kids: If anyone slept badly, this becomes a rest day. That is the right call at this altitude.
days.seasonal: Some side valleys have closed in winter and reopen with the peak season. Confirm what is actually open.
days.wet: Hotel balcony if the first park day was already wet and long.

days.experience: A Tibetan village walk close to town, kept short.
days.highlight: The valley outside the park fence
days.kids: Flat walking and a chance to buy nothing.
days.seasonal: Be polite in monasteries. A short visit is better than a tour speech.

days.experience: Fly back to Chengdu. Do not sightsee.
days.optional: A pharmacy and a calm dinner
days.highlight: Coming down to a lower city before the long-haul flight
days.transfer: Reverse the inbound flight and road transfer. Build in a buffer. Mountain airports delay.
days.seasonal: Do not fly home the same day you leave Jiuzhaigou.
days.wet: The buffer day is the point.

days.optional: A last panda only if the flight is in the evening and everyone is well
days.kids: No new attraction if the flight is before noon.
days.transfer: International connections from Chengdu. Seven seats.
